 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. San Francisco 49ers quarterback Mac Jones doesn't say much about his personal life, but he finally offered a look behind the curtain during his team's bye week.
 It was reported earlier this year that Jones is no longer dating Sophie Scott. Rumors about them being together first surfaced when they were students at the University of Alabama. Scott supported Jones during the first few years of his career with the New England Patriots.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement While it's unclear when Jones and Scott went their separate ways, he opened up about his dating life on George Kittle's podcast.
 For starters, Jones said his biggest green flag is that he's "attracted to smart, smart, ladies." As for any deal-breakers, let's just say he's not interested in going out to eat seafood.
 "Just don't go to a seafood spot with me," Jones said, via the New York Post. "I'm not allergic to anything, I just don't like it."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Nov 2, 2025; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; San Francisco 49ers quarterback Mac Jones (10) warms up prior to a game against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images© Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images.
 What's next for Mac's career?
 Jones is currently the backup to 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy. He started eight games for San Francisco in 2025, completing 69.6% of his passes for 2,151 yards with 13 touchdowns and six interceptions.
 Although the trade deadline is coming up, 49ers general manager John Lynch is not expected to move Jones.
 "I think back to [former 49ers coach] Bill Walsh; maybe he was on to something when he had Joe Montana but he also brought Steve Young in here," Lynch said, via NBC Sports Bay Area . "It's a good position to be in, a position of strength, and it provides opportunities in a number of ways, the most important way being that you're well insulated in the event something ever were to happen. And then there also are opportunities you receive calls and then you make decisions accordingly. But we love our situation at quarterback."
